[Five Practical Tips to Parenting, from a Quantitative Drug Developer](https://medium.com/@andy.stein/five-practical-tips-to-parenting-from-a-quantitative-drug-developer-bda0cc794142),
by Andy Stein on Medium, 4 October 2021.

**Much of how a child turns out is outside a parent's control, so the post
recommends being present, trying things and watching a few signals.** It draws
on Bryan Caplan's *Selfish Reasons to Have More Kids*, Emily Oster's
*Cribsheet* and the US Air Force's discovery of the flaw of averages.

1. **Uncertainty and lack of control.** Genetics and environment decide much of
   the outcome, and children tend to turn out like their genetic parents. The
   best a parent can do is be present, love and listen.
2. **Variability.** No child is average in every respect, so a study about the
   average child is a starting point. Try things and keep what works.
3. **Biomarkers.** Among all the rules and opinions, what a parent needs is a
   signal that something is really wrong. A baby whose weight stays within
   reasonable bounds is almost certainly well nourished.
4. **Childhood wounding is necessary.** Leaving abuse aside, no parent meets
   every want and need, and overprotection makes a wound of its own.
5. **Memories can be influenced.** How children remember their parents depends
   largely on how loving, communicative and conflict-prone the family was.
